verdict.text: This narrow round only checked whether f1 is fixed, and it is.
The explanation page now limits the "what is due" and read-and-search-only claims to the in-session `/audit`.
It says CI runs three audits, can run shell commands, and sends each audit's findings to the job summary and to that audit's own issue.
Each of those claims matches the code.
The gates are green on the tree under review.
Ran `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree.
Lint, format, tests, integration and eval rows r1 to r3 all pass.
This matches the fingerprint bound to this round.

Read the diff of `docs/explanation/why-one-hook-and-report-only-audits.md` and checked it against the code: The three audits named on the page match the workflow's `audit: [docs-vs-code, okf-vs-code, okf-vs-docs]` matrix.
The shell claim matches `run_shell` in the tool list in `action/agent.py`, and the module docstring ("so it can use the scripts skills ship").
The issue claim matches the publish matrix, which gives each audit a different `title` and passes it with `--title`.
The job summary claim matches `publish`, which writes to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` in each publish leg.
"Neither edits" and "never marks verified" still hold, because the agent only reports.
The audit paragraph in `docs/explanation/why-one-hook-and-report-only-audits.md` is now accurate, as checked above.
